🌸 SPRING EQUINOX EXPLAINED — MARCH 20, 2026
📅 March 15, 2026

In just 5 days, something extraordinary happens to our entire planet at once. On March 20 at 14:46 UTC, the Sun crosses directly above Earth's equator, and for one brief moment, every place on Earth shares nearly the same length of day and night.

🌍 What Is Actually Happening?
Earth orbits the Sun tilted at 23.5 degrees on its axis. For most of the year, one hemisphere leans toward the Sun and gets more light, while the other leans away. At the equinox, neither hemisphere is tilted toward or away. The Sun's rays strike the equator perpendicularly, and the terminator line dividing day from night runs perfectly from pole to pole. Both poles receive sunlight simultaneously for the only time all year.

☀️ Why Day and Night Are NOT Perfectly Equal
The word equinox comes from the Latin for "equal night," but the actual length of day and night is not exactly 12 hours each. Atmospheric refraction bends sunlight over the horizon before the Sun geometrically rises, adding several extra minutes of daylight. The equinox day also varies slightly by latitude: on the equator it is closest to a perfect 12-12 split, while polar regions see a slightly longer day.

🌐 Two Seasons Begin Simultaneously
Spring begins in the Northern Hemisphere: days grow longer, the Sun rises higher, temperatures climb, and plants bloom. At the exact same moment, the Southern Hemisphere enters astronomical autumn: days shorten and the Sun tracks lower across the sky toward winter. One moment divides two seasons across an entire planet.

🏛️ Ancient Cultures Built Monuments to This Day
At Chichen Itza in Mexico, the Pyramid of Kukulcan was deliberately aligned so that at equinox, the Sun casts a series of triangular shadows down the staircase, creating the visual illusion of a feathered serpent descending the pyramid. Stonehenge, the Sphinx at Giza, and the temples of Angkor Wat are all similarly oriented to the equinox Sun. Civilizations separated by oceans and millennia all recognized this moment as a cosmic hinge point.

Fun fact: After March 20, the Northern Hemisphere will gain roughly 2 to 4 extra minutes of daylight every single day until the summer solstice on June 21. If you are in New York, you will have gained almost 4 hours of extra daylight by midsummer.

Do you notice the shift in light after the equinox? Where in the world will you be watching the Sun rise exactly due east on March 20?
